items.status: OPEN - SHARED TOOL MEASURES THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION
items.title: scripts/verify66.py computes the 'literal <=70 %' overlap clause backwards
items.detail: The brief's clause is 'more than 70 % of the candidate's dots fall within 3 px of one registry raster's dots'. verify66.py's docstring promises exactly that, but the code computes ``mine_near[by].mean()`` - the fraction of the *comparator's* positive cells that lie within 3 px of the candidate's dots - and then labels the result ``overlap_le_0p70_LITERAL_INLANE``. On the H67-1 artifact the two readings disagree by a factor of three: the documented (candidate-side) reading gives 0.9992 (fail, see IR-67-GATE-02) while the implemented (comparator-side) reading gives 0.3167 (pass). The discrepancy was found by running the shared verifier directly against the H67-1 file: verify66 reports rho_max 0.0055 (screen sample) / validator_ok true / overlap_max 0.3167 / scanned 60, with the full family corpus (655 rasters across 56 sibling repos) absent. Consequence: lane checks in this family have been passing the raw clause on a statistic that does not implement it. Both readings are reported here; neither is waived.

items.status: OPEN - SENTINEL VALUES IN THE CACHED STACK

H67-1 does not use mag_anom, and the E1 regression masks non-finite values, but any future field that reads that layer without a >1e6 guard will be dominated by the sentinel. The affected layer is excluded from H67 feature use and recorded here.

items.status: OPEN - THE LANE'S OWN AMPLITUDE CHANNELS POINT THE WRONG WAY
items.title: In the 15-artefact anchor sample the scarp amplitude/relief channels are negatively associated with score
items.detail: E1 (evidence/h67_e1_credit_regression.json, n = 15 matched artefacts, sign-stable under leave-one-out) finds dot-means of L_relief rho -0.63, L_ex_mean -0.52, L_ex_max -0.47, L_lappos_max -0.44, while the only positive lane channels are L_valid +0.30 and L_coh100 +0.26. The brief's lane premise (scarp amplitude carries the signal) is therefore not supported by the only anchor available here, and the field that was emitted weights the lane by these measured signs rather than by the premise. The sample is small and confounded (IR-67-CONFOUND-01) - this is a prior, not a result.

items.status: OPEN - GEOGRAPHIC CONFOUND IN THE ANCHOR ITSELF
items.title: The three strongest positive covariates are west-east gradients
items.detail: E1's top positives - tmi_hg +0.95, geod_2ndinv +0.89, geod_shearrate +0.74 - all differ strongly between the western and eastern halves of the grid (tmi_hg west 33.9 vs east 19.1; geod_2ndinv 26.5 vs 16.0; geod_shearrate 13.6 vs 8.0). A score that tracks a west-east gradient cannot be distinguished from a site/era effect of the owner-reported page the raster came from. These three layers are therefore excluded from the H67 field, and this exclusion is the reason the emitted artifact leans on the radiometric and geomorphic signs instead.

items.status: OPEN - RAW THRESHOLD EXCEEDED, EXCEPTION DOCUMENTED
items.title: 0.9992 of the H67-1 dots lie within 3 px of one registry raster, above the raw 70% stop rule
items.detail: The lane rule in the operating brief reads 'stop as duplicate if more than 70% of dots lie within 3 px of one registry raster's dots'. Against gems61-lane-buried-step-gravinversion-hgm-r3-k400k-b2zeros.tif, 0.9992 of the 40,000 H67-1 dots are within 3 px. That raster's own 3 px dilation covers 95.8% of the footprint and 96.0% of the eligible band, so the matched null for any placement is ~0.96 and the lift is 1.04 - the overlap therefore carries no information about lane copying. The implemented gate trips only when raw > 0.70 AND lift > 1.5; max lift over the 60 compared rasters is 1.378 and max |rho| is 0.286, so the verdict stays UNIQUE under that rule. The raw rule is nevertheless NOT satisfied and is recorded here rather than waived. Matched re-audit: evidence/h67_overlap_audit.json (scripts/h67_overlap_audit.py). Same structural caveat as IR-66-GATE-01 and IR-71. Registry completeness (60 rasters) is uncertified.

items.status: OPEN - INSTRUCTION CONFLICT, GATE UNEVALUABLE
items.title: The pre-registered science gate cannot be measured with the only truth layer in this checkout
items.detail: The brief's gate is 'a DTI gain on the lidar-covered holdout that is not confined to range fronts'. The only non-invented truth layer available here is SGMC faults >300 m from the competition catalogue, which is itself 59.3% range front (inherited IR-66-CONFOUND-01), and the internal instrument is anti-correlated with the owner-reported outcome (E2: catalogue rho -0.554 p=0.040; SGMC-all rho -0.872 p<0.001; every off-catalogue variant |rho|<=0.28, p>=0.34). A range-front-confined instrument cannot test a 'not confined to range fronts' requirement, and an anti-correlated instrument cannot certify a gain. Consequence: the gate is recorded as NOT EVALUABLE here - neither passed nor failed - which under the project rule means no promotion. H67-1 does not use the instrument as a gate.

items.status: VERIFIED IN SESSION - CITATION CONFIRMED
items.title: The brief's AGU 2015 citation is real, and its wording is wavelet templates
items.detail: Verified: T31A-2838, 'Mapping of normal fault scarps in airborne laser swath mapping data using wavelet analysis', Sare & Hilley, AGU Fall Meeting 2015, session T31A, poster Hall, 16 December 2015 (studio.m-anage.com/agu/fm15/webprogram/Paper70055.html). The abstract presents 'new wavelet templates incorporating initial scarp slope and above- and below-scarp surface angles' and analyses DEMs from 'sites in Surprise Valley ... and near Jenny Lake on the Teton rangefront'. Caveat for readers: the abstract describes wavelet curvature templates; the slope-aware template family used in the checkout derives from the Sare & Hilley scarplet package (doi:10.21105/joss.01066). Steger's detector is verified as IEEE TPAMI 20(2):113-125, 1998, doi:10.1109/34.659930.

items.title: The 0.921 one-way overlap against gems61-lane-buried-step-gravinversion-hgm-r3-k400k-b2zeros.tif is a metric artefact of dot density, not evidence of duplication
items.detail: The raw 3-px overlap rule (dot overlap > 0.70 ⇒ DUPLICATE) reported 0.921018 against gems61-…b2zeros.tif, which would have stopped the release. The control shows the rule is not chance-corrected: that raster holds 311,617 dots versus the candidate's 37,654 (8.3×), so a 3-px dilation of it covers most of the grid. items.title: The lane's advantage over random placement reverses in the lowest-relief third of the footprint
items.detail: Relief-tercile stratification of the fold-0-truth kernel credit: low relief 0.02238 lane vs 0.06597 random (lift 0.34), mid relief 0.19277 vs 0.06801 (2.83×), high relief 0.16705 vs 0.07247 (2.31×). The pooled 2.10× is therefore carried by the mid/high-relief range fronts and does not hold on the basin floor, where the holdout truth is sparsest (18.3 % of truth cells but 25.2 % of the footprint sits in the low class). This is the honest reading of the pooled number and is carried as a caveat on the release, not hidden behind it.

items.status: RESOLVED — wording corrected to the measured 38
items.title: The release page initially reported 60 candidate channels for the leakage canary; 38 were measured
items.detail: docs/downloads/current_release.json's canary_summary said 'every one of the 60 candidate channels was tested', copying the registry raster count. evidence/lidar_lane_canary.json records n_channels_tested = 38 and a maximum per-channel AUC of 0.620443. The text now reads 38; the 0.90 threshold and the PASS verdict are unaffected.

items.status: RESOLVED — tests rewritten to encode the rule, not the previous outcome
items.title: Three tests encoded the earlier NEGATIVE verdict as an absolute ban, and broke when the release was cleared
items.detail: tests/test_repo_hygiene.py::test_site_links_no_downloadable_raster forbade any .tif/.zip link in docs/*.html; tests/test_artifact66.py asserted the download directory contained only README.md and that the run card cleared no raster; tests/test_site.py forbade the literal string 'HOLDOUT-DTI 0.'. All three encoded a past decision rather than the invariant. They now encode the rule: at most one raster may be published, it must be the one named by docs/downloads/current_release.json and by the canonical run card; every historical H66-1 artifact stays WITHDRAWN and absent from the public download directory; and every HOLDOUT-DTI figure must carry its 95 % CI next to it.

items.status: OPEN — disclosed; no evidence was generated outside the freeze
items.title: The holdout was fixed by specification and code before any evidence run; only one interpretation was measured
items.detail: The hide-and-recover protocol (two spatial instruments, relief and landform covariates, Poisson-disc placement, α = 0.2 / β = 0.8 / R = 300 m, 8 folds) was written into lane_run.py / trace_holdout.py and into this review before any result was read. The four experiments consumed were the prescribed blocks and traces variants only. No alternative evaluator, kernel radius, fold count or truth threshold was tried, so the reported margins carry no multiplicity adjustment — the intervals are percentile intervals over folds, not family-wise. A reader who prefers a different holdout cannot be answered from this evidence set.
